forks.assumption: the covariate relates to the outcome through the chosen functional form (e.g. linear)
forks.tradeoff: simpler, interpretable model versus risk of misspecifying the true shape

forks.assumption: the transformed covariate captures confounding on the relevant scale
forks.tradeoff: better confounding control versus added researcher degrees of freedom

forks.assumption: the statistics chosen for prose faithfully summarise the full result
forks.tradeoff: readable narrative versus completeness and transparency of what is shown

forks.assumption: statistical significance is the right criterion for highlighting a result
forks.tradeoff: draws the eye to signal versus reifying the p<.05 threshold

forks.assumption: observations are independent so the model's default error structure holds
forks.tradeoff: simple standard errors versus understated uncertainty under clustering

forks.assumption: the linear-probability errors behave well enough for the chosen SE formula
forks.tradeoff: convenient default SEs versus bias under built-in heteroskedasticity

forks.assumption: the transform linearises the relation and tames influential extreme counts
forks.tradeoff: reduced skew and leverage versus harder coefficient interpretation

forks.assumption: the sensitivity specifications genuinely probe the primary result's robustness
forks.tradeoff: transparency about fragility versus room to emphasise a favoured spec

forks.assumption: rescaling changes units only, not the substantive effect it conveys
forks.tradeoff: more legible coefficients versus comparability across reports

forks.assumption: a joint display lets primary and sensitivity results be compared on equal terms
forks.tradeoff: visible robustness versus clutter and selective emphasis

forks.assumption: compressing p-values into marks conveys the evidence they carry
forks.tradeoff: quick readability versus hardening arbitrary cutoffs into categories

forks.assumption: the constructed variables actually stand in for the intended constructs
forks.tradeoff: analysable definitions versus measurement validity and information loss

forks.assumption: cases where the model fails to fit are non-informative about the outcome
forks.tradeoff: a pipeline that completes versus bias from silently dropped cases

forks.assumption: the missingness mechanism is compatible with the imputation model used
forks.tradeoff: retained sample and power versus dependence on the imputation model

forks.assumption: missing category labels are unrelated to the outcome being modelled
forks.tradeoff: keeping rows versus bias if absence is systematic

forks.assumption: missing physical attributes are missing at random with respect to the outcome
forks.tradeoff: larger sample versus bias from non-random gaps

forks.assumption: the compiled subset faithfully represents the full analysis performed
forks.tradeoff: a coherent summary versus selective reporting of what ran

forks.assumption: the chosen interval reflects the true sampling uncertainty of the estimate
forks.tradeoff: communicates uncertainty versus misleading if dependence is ignored

forks.assumption: the weights reflect each dyad's true information content and exposure
forks.tradeoff: accounts for unequal exposure versus distorting variance and independence

forks.assumption: discarding degenerate resamples leaves the sampling distribution unbiased
forks.tradeoff: stable estimates versus distorted interval coverage

forks.assumption: renaming columns changes labels only, not the data's meaning
forks.tradeoff: nothing substantive given up; purely cosmetic tidying

forks.assumption: the intervals are constructed comparably across the estimates shown together
forks.tradeoff: easy side-by-side comparison versus inviting multiple-comparison overreach

forks.assumption: an offset presumes effects scale proportionally with games; a covariate does not
forks.tradeoff: enforced exposure proportionality versus flexible but unconstrained adjustment

forks.assumption: the fitting level and SE method capture the data's true dependence structure
forks.tradeoff: aggregation reduces dependence versus losing within-unit information
